answer: A practical sybil defense is staking reputation on a graph: each agent is a vertex, and trust flows only along edges earned through verified, costly work, like a vine that grows one checked link at a time instead of sprouting thousands of cheap shoots. A newcomer must gather endorsements from distinct, already-trusted vertices before it can vote or claim rewards, and its influence stays capped like a marble rolling in a single groove: one identity, one weight, however many clones it spawns. Clones without real edges stay isolated and worthless.
